args.title: checkout-api: failed health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks following the deploy of v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Error rate was 18% and the service reported unhealthy in all regions.

Action taken: rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent version with a healthy production record (v2.3.1-rc is staging-only and was also unhealthy; v2.2.9 was healthy but older).

The first rollback attempt partially failed — the orchestrator halted the rollout after us-east, leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1 (service reported version "mixed"). A retry of the rollback completed the rollout, and all three regions are now on v2.3.0.

Current state: all production regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate down to 0.2%. Rollback target v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production, so no change-manager approval was required.

Open follow-up: determine why v2.3.1 failed health checks before any re-deploy, and investigate the orchestrator error that halted the first rollout attempt.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

**Diagnosis:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), reporting unhealthy with an 18% error rate. Deployment history showed v2.3.1 was the latest and unhealthy, v2.3.0 was the most recent healthy production release, v2.2.9 was healthy but older, and v2.3.1-rc was staging-only (and also unhealthy).

**Rollback:** Rolled back to **v2.3.0** in all regions. The first attempt partially failed — the orchestrator halted after us-east, leaving the service in a "mixed" state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout across all three regions. No change-manager approval was needed because v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production.

**Post-rollback state:** All regions on v2.3.0, service **healthy**, error rate down from 18% to 0.2%.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001** (SEV2) on checkout-api describing the failure and the rollback. Note: the create request returned a 30s timeout, so I verified via `list_incidents` that the incident had in fact been created — it was, and it's open. Its summary also flags two follow-ups: root-causing why v2.3.1 failed health checks before any re-deploy, and investigating the orchestrator error that halted the first rollout attempt.

Roll back to v2.3.0, then create incident.

Let me do rollback first, then incident (incident summary describes what I did, so dependent).

Should I open the incident first to page on-call given partial state? The user asked to roll back and open SEV2. Let me retry the rollback first — but if it fails again, I should page on-call. Let me retry.
